Hi Alex — great to meet yesterday, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) Summary of fit
- Primary goal: structured extraction from unstructured financial reports and automated Q&A with table output (JSON).
- Initial impression: your dataset looks like a good fit for a mid-sized decoder model with function-calling + strong schema validation. We think two model families are worth evaluating: Redwood-Infer-3B-qa (lower latency) and Redwood-Infer-7B-quant (higher quality, quantized for cost).

2) Deliverables we can provide this week
- Prompt set v1 (attached) showing extraction prompts + canonical output schema. [attachment: prompt_set_v1.csv (text/csv)]
- Eval runner config with function-calling retries and schema enforcement examples. [attachment: eval_runner-config.json (application/json)]
- Benchmark doc + runner link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-findata-evals

3) Key questions / asks for you
- Please share a 200–500 document sample (anonymized) for model-fit runs — link or S3 credentials are fine.
- Are there any strict schema compliance requirements (e.g., nested arrays prohibited, numeric rounding rules)?

4) Next steps
- If you can share sample data, Dev (cc'd) will run a short 24–48h experiment across the two model variants with JSON schema checks + retries on failure.
- We'll tee up a 30-minute follow-up once results are in to review failure modes, latency, and cost tradeoffs.

Notes about tool/function calling: we recommend enforcing a strict JSON schema validator on the client side and adding a light retry policy for ephemeral model errors. We'll include an example validator in the eval runner config.

Thanks — feel free to add Emily or anyone else on your side.

Thanks Alex — got it on the schema constraints. A couple quick technical notes on our eval approach and the retry/validation policy we suggest: 

- Validation pipeline: each model response goes through a two-step check: 1) JSON parse + strict schema validation (we use Ajv in the runner), 2) semantic checks (e.g., all required fields present, numeric ranges, id uniqueness).
- Retry policy: for transient parse errors or missing optional fields we attempt up to 2 automatic retries with exponential backoff and slightly different decoding params (top_p/temperature). If required fields are missing after retries we flag as a hard failure for manual inspection. Retries are idempotent because we compare final validated id + hash; duplicates are dropped at aggregation.
- Function-calling: we instrument the function call layer to prefer structured responses (we pass function schema). If model returns plain text, runner will attempt to coerce to JSON and apply the schema; this is considered a soft failure and will trigger a retry.

I've attached a minimal eval_runner-config.json showing the retry window and schema snippet used in the run. [attachment: eval_runner-config.json (application/json)]

If you share the S3 link+creds I'll kick off a small run (n=250) on Redwood-Infer-3B-qa and Redwood-Infer-7B-quant. Expected timeline: 24-48 hours for initial metrics (precision/recall on extracted fields, schema pass rate, median latency).

Cheers,

Schema pass-rate will depend largely on prompt engineering; Dev's retry policy should keep soft-failures under 5% in many cases.
- I'll attach a short cost estimate for the 24h Dedicated pilot and a note on how quantization impacts unit cost. [attachment: cost-estimate.pdf (application/pdf)]
